Av3 writer liveness is judged by process identity (swamp-club#3564) (#3184)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-17T20:37:19Zdatastorefix

What's Changed

  • fix(datastore): v3 writer liveness is judged by process identity (swamp-club#3564) (#3184)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3564 (v3 bug hunt group 1). Whether a v3 writer is still alive was judged wrong in seven ways. One rule now decides it everywhere: the writer lease, the writer marker, the checkout sidecar (writer.checkout.json) and the commit outbox.

Each record names its writer's process identity: processHostIdentity() (the hostname plus the pid namespace), the kernel boot id, and the process start time. The start time is read over FFI, because the compiled binary may not read /proc directly. On macOS it comes from sysctl(KERN_PROC_PID), which also answers for zombies and for other users' processes. judgeRecordedProcess (src/domain/datastore_v3/process_liveness.ts) gives one of three verdicts:

  • gone: the pid is absent, a zombie, or started at a different time than recorded, or it is this process's own pid on a record whose token isn't this process's. The holder is taken over, or its checkout recovered, at once.
  • alive: the writer's checkout stays protected whatever the TTL says.
  • unknown: the record is from another host, pid namespace or boot, a boot id is missing on Linux or macOS, or the record predates this change. Only TTL plus skew and the fence apply; such a writer is never judged gone. A writer always recognises its own checkout sidecar by the fence it wrote it with, so a missing boot id never makes it skip its

What's Changed

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3565: four bugs found in a v3 replication bug hunt, which went live for S3 and GCS v3 datastores with #3180. One of them was an S1.

  • S1, acknowledged commits lost. A lease retake while serve's sidecar replacement was inside its restore let the stale restore be marked current and start a lineage at the old fence. The datastore forked, and readers followed the other writer's lineage, so serve's acknowledged commit was lost. Now:
  • A retake makes the in-flight replacement stale: it marks nothing current and starts no lineage or sidecar at its old fence. Its read model is still rebuilt.
  • ensureV3CopyCurrent re-checks right before it marks the copy current.
  • prepareV3WriterLineage refuses to start a lineage below one a newer writer started.
  • Serve wedge (V3-54). A replacement asked for while one was running was dropped, so after the retake serve refused every commit until restart. Now:
  • The request reruns once the running replacement settles.
  • The probe also replaces a copy that is not current.
  • stop() waits for any rerun.
  • Unconfirmed commits (V3-40). The exit-75 message now says the kept commits replicate only if this checkout writes next, and are lost if another checkout writes first. A restore

𝗗 release v20261016.225135.0-sha.4a68e87b𝗖𝗟 4a68e87b𝗣 #3181𝗔 lab#3552

Arun gc and data gc cost the same however much history is kept, and serve's automatic retention pass is bounded (swamp-club#3535) (#3178)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-16T20:56:58Zgcfix

What's Changed

  • fix(gc): run gc and data gc cost the same however much history is kept, and serve's automatic retention pass is bounded (swamp-club#3535) (#3178)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3535 and explains the slow pass in swamp-club#3518.

Every swamp run gc and data gc, on every datastore, cost (files deleted) × (entries kept beside them). After each deleted run or output file, cleanupEmptyParentDirs read the whole parent directory into an array just to check whether it was empty. With a large kept history, especially outputs, where one type and method share one directory, a small backlog took minutes and a large one hours. That is what made #3518's 26-minute pass slow.

  • Cleanup without listing. cleanupEmptyParentDirs removes each parent directory with a non-recursive remove, which fails on a directory that still has entries, and never lists it. A not-empty error ends the cleanup quietly on every OS, with no error-code matching. A symlinked directory keeps the old read-through check, because a remove unlinks a link whatever its target holds. All ten callers keep their behaviour.
  • Full listings before deleting. deleteOlderThan reads its run listings in full before deleting anything. Without this, step 1 made run gc delete only about 60% of expired runs per call on macOS: a failed remove of a directory makes a walk still open on it skip entries. An audit of src/ found no other caller that deletes while lazily walking the directory it cleans.
Docs changed: design/surfaces/repo.md

2026-10-16T20:15:38Zextensionsfix

What's Changed

  • fix(extensions): the first bundle per deno cache runs alone so concurrent bundles never race to install esbuild; fix the flaky and Windows-only test failures on main (swamp-club#3556, swamp-club#3560) (#3174)

Summary

The scheduled flaky-test job and the Windows Compatibility job on main were red. This fixes every failure they showed, plus swamp-club#3560.

Cause, product: when a Deno cache has no esbuild, the first deno bundle installs it. Two bundles started at once on that cache both install it, and one can fail with failed to copy esbuild binary … (os error 2). This race was behind two flaky tests:

  • the swamp-club#3313 pull-conflict test on Linux;
  • the intermittent extension_tree_index failure on Windows, which hit 6 of 34 runs.

A user's first push, install or parallel load on a fresh machine can hit the same race.

Fix: bundleExtension now runs the first bundle per DENO_DIR alone, through a small runFirstAlone gate.

  • A bundle whose output names the esbuild copy failure (another process installing into the same cache) is retried once, inside the gate.
  • The gate stays closed if that retry also loses, so the next bundle installs alone.
  • Each run starts its own timeout, and an abort ends a wait behind the first bundle.

Test-only fixes:

  • macOS and Windows, every run: four resolveExtensionFiles tests still expected the symlink-resolved workflow path that #3536 stopped reporting (/private/var on macOS, `runneradmi

What's Changed

  • fix(vault): MockVaultProvider.get and delete reject for a missing key instead of throwing synchronously (swamp-club#3559) (#3171)

Summary

MockVaultProvider.get() and delete() are typed to return a promise, but for a missing key they threw before returning one. A caller that awaits the call can't tell the difference, but one that chains .catch() on the result gets an uncaught synchronous throw. Every other built-in provider rejects.

  • src/domain/vaults/mock_vault_provider.ts: the missing-key branch now returns Promise.reject(new Error(...)) with the same message. Both methods stay non-async, because require-await rejects an async method with no await.
  • src/domain/vaults/mock_vault_provider_test.ts: the two missing-key tests switch from assertThrows to assertRejects. assertRejects fails with "Function throws when expected to reject" when the callback throws synchronously, so the tests now guard against the old behavior coming back.

Not a regression: the old tests asserted the synchronous throw. The vault conformance suite doesn't catch it, because it awaits get() inside try/catch, where a synchronous throw and a rejection look the same. Tightening the suite would change the contract for third-party vault authors, so it's left out of this PR.

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3553.

On a v3 datastore, a command whose commit was refused (another process took the writer lease, version-live, version-reused), whose root was abandoned, or whose end failed left the files its repositories wrote in its checkout for good. That checkout then showed data the datastore does not hold. swamp-club#3532 made it visible: a refused version now sits on its own path, so nothing ever replaced it. swamp-uat's breakglass test (lock release --force --model mid-run loses no write… on filesystem-v3) has failed on every Datastore UAT run since.

  • A unit reports dropped work. A v3 unit is *touched* once a repository writes into it: the write signal (signalChange, stageTyped before its builder runs) or any change it records, including a committed child's batches. A touched unit that drops work tells its handle, with its root's open time.
  • The command recovers before it exits. closeV3Datastores decides, while the lease and copy state are still present, whether this process still writes the datastore. That means the lease is held and current, the commit store's fence is not above its own, and, while replicating, its copy is current. When swamp extension pull <parent> hit a file conflict in one of the parent's dependencies, answering y installed the parent but silently skipped the dependency. The dependency got no lockfile entry, its local files were left as they were, and nothing reported it.

Cause: pullExtension (src/cli/commands/extension_pull.ts) retried with force after removing only the parent's name from alreadyPulled. The first attempt had already marked the dependency (installLocked / applyInstall in src/libswamp/extensions/pull.ts), so the retry skipped it.

Marks a caller made before the pull are kept, and every extension the failed attempt reached is installed again. Dependencies the first attempt had already committed have lockfile entries and are skipped as before.

Answering N to a dependency's conflict still leaves the parent installed. That is a separate defect and will be filed on its own.

Fixes swamp-club#3519. During a long serve GC pass (swamp-club#3518), remote steps whose methods finished and whose resources were saved were recorded as failed with The operation was aborted due to timeout.

Cause: the worker aborted every unary data-plane request after 60s. A method's final POST /data/resource was already queued at serve. Serve saved it once GC let go, but by then the worker had given up and the runner had reported the dispatch as an error.

  • Unary writes (resource write and delete, writer open, line append, finalize) now wait up to 15 minutes (DATA_PLANE_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS).
  • Reads keep the 60s bound, and bulk uploads and bundle fetches stay unbounded.
  • Dispatch cancel still aborts any request at once.
  • Writes are not retried: serve's write routes are not idempotent (each POST creates a version or appends a line).
  • No protocol change, so mixed worker and serve versions keep working.
  • When the client's own deadline fires, the error now names the route, e.g. Serve did not answer POST /data/resource within 900s; serve may still have saved this write. The bare DOMException text is gone, and a cancelled step keeps its own abort reason.

The CommitOutbox port, and the unit of work's SinkOutbox, now split remove into two operations:

  • settle stays relaxed. It is used only after a commit landed: by the unit's landed path and by recovery's landed or already-landed outcomes.

  • the unit's refusal, abandon and failed-end paths;
  • the sink's owed-removal retry at close (every owed key is retried durably);
  • every recovery drop and unreadable entry;
  • the shared-outbox drop when replication starts.

Why this goes beyond the call sites the issue names: splitting the port makes every caller choose, and recovery drops are the same class of bug. Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3485.

On S3 and GCS, a run that lost its model lock refused its push and relied on a best-effort refresh pull to replace its data versions in the cache. When the datastore was unreachable, the pull failed and the refused versions stayed dirty, so the next sync pushed them. Either data from a run reported as failed reached every clone, or, after a breakglass, it overwrote the new holder's version.

The refusal now discards the versions the push would publish, before it throws:

So each removed file, and the latest marker, is restored as the datastore holds it, read with fetchContent under a 10 s budget. A file the datastore lacks stays removed. Without the restore, a push-only sync after a breakglass would delete the new holder's same-numbered version.
  • Refresh pull. The best-effort refresh pull still runs, then the catalog is invalidated.
  • Unchanged. Error code model_lock_lost and exit code 1. The message now says the run's data was discarded. Filesystem, v3 and lock-held pushes do not change.

2026-10-14T23:40:50Zextensionsfix

What's Changed

  • fix(extensions): extensions pushed from Windows pack folders as 0755 and files as 0644, so registry scoring can read them (swamp-club#3484) (#3130)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3484, reported by @mtaylor (swamp-club) with a precise repro. Thank you!

When swamp extension push ran on Windows, every folder in the archive was packed as drw-rw-rw- (0666) and every file as -rw-rw-rw-. Windows has no POSIX modes, so Deno reports 0o666 for every file and folder, and createTarGz copied that value into each tar header. The registry scorer runs tar -xzf on Linux, which applies the archive's modes. It can't enter a folder without the execute bit, so every extension published from Windows failed scoring with No manifest.yaml found in tarball.

  • On Windows, createTarGz now records folders as 0755 and files as 0644. These are the modes a Unix push records with the usual umask.
  • On Linux and macOS it still records the real modes, including executable bits, so pushes from those systems are unchanged.
  • createTarGz takes an optional os parameter (default Deno.build.os) so the Windows path is tested on every OS.

Extensions already published from Windows stay unscored until their author pushes a new version. Their stored archives keep 0666 folders, and rescoring reuses the same archive. Fixing modes during extraction is a scorer change and belongs in swamp-club.

Test Plan

  • New test `createTarGz: packs folders 0o755 and files 0o644 on Window

  • Only a lowercase UUID is accepted as output.

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3405. After a serve restart, a worker's enroll call timed out while serve was still recording the enrollment. The socket's close handler found no worker to disconnect, so the enrollment then admitted the closed socket as a live worker. As a result:

The dead session (src/serve/worker_gateway.ts)

Why enrollment was slow

  • Every write serve makes about workers looked its definition up by name across the whole repo, parsing every file under models/. This covers token redeem, worker enroll and status, and dispatch leases. A new fleet member costs about four of these full passes, and enrollments run one at a time.

each second. Before #3105, on #3105 and with this change, entries all

go stale and are healed the same way, in sweeps whenever some reader

catches a mismatch. How many stay stale at the end of a burst depends

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3420, a security regression from #3376 (swamp #3081), on stable since a3fab18f.

Since #3376, push reads each entry point's module graph with deno info. deno info followed a symlinked model and parsed its target. An unparseable target became a missing module carrying deno's parse error, which quotes the target's source, and it dropped out of the file list. So the safety gate never saw the symlink, and push printed the target's first line (root:x:0:0… for /etc/passwd) as a compilation error.

What push does now

  • Entry points are checked with lstat before anything reads them. The bare-specifier scan, deno info and the bundler never follow one.
  • Every other symlink deno info reaches is removed from the graph before the graph is used (withoutSymlinkedModules, a pure domain function). Everything it alone leads to goes with it, and so does any error recorded for it.
  • Each symlink is listed for the safety gate, which refuses it by the symlink rule before bundling, as 68e0ed7d did, in log and --json (errors.safety). A symlink to a valid module outside the repository is not packaged. It is now refused by the symlink rule instead of the containment error.
  • The checks that run before the safety gate never read a symlink either. Content metadata skips one, so a type the target declares cannot

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3374.

Indexing a new or edited extension source imported its bundle into the command's own isolate to read and validate the export. Whatever the source did at import therefore happened in every command, including listings that never use the extension:

  • a source that called Deno.exit ended the command (exit 3, empty output);
  • a source with a never-settling top-level await hung it;
  • a source that printed put its output ahead of the JSON document.

An exit or a hang repeated on every command, because the source never reached an indexed state.

Index-time imports now probe the bundle instead of loading it. A probe imports the bundle in a Deno worker and answers with plain data: the exported type, version and description, or why there is none. The type is registered lazy and is imported into the command's isolate only when it is used.

What changed

  • BundleProber port (src/domain/extensions/bundle_prober.ts) and its worker implementation (src/infrastructure/runtime/worker_bundle_prober.ts, bundle_probe_worker.ts). The worker entry point is added to the --include list in scripts/compile.ts.

What's Changed

  • fix(datastore): a stray or unpadded key under _control/writer/ no longer wedges the v3 writer lease (swamp-club#3375) (#3083)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3375.

parseWriterLeaseKey accepted a fence of any number of digits, while fenceKey() refuses one above MAX_FENCE (10^12 - 1):

  • A stray key wedged the lease. A _control/writer/fence-1000000000000 file made readWriterLeaseRecords throw a generic Error, so acquire, inspect, swamp datastore lock status and swamp datastore lock release --force all failed until the file was deleted by hand.
  • Unpadded keys aliased padded ones. fence-5 parsed as fence 5 but is a different key from fence-000000000005, so putIfAbsent on one did not exclude the other (a stray fence-5 made acquire skip to fence 6; a stray released-5 would have released the real fence 5).

The parser now accepts only keys of exactly FENCE_DIGITS (12) digits whose fence is from 1 to MAX_FENCE, the exact inverse of the key constructors. Every other key is ignored, as unrelated keys already were. All lease readers (readWriterLeaseRecords, renewal #check, takeover #prune) share the parser, so every entry point is fixed together. swamp itself only ever writes 12-digit in-range keys, so no existing lease changes behaviour.

The design doc's v3 writer lease section now states which keys are lease records.

Test Plan

  • writer_lease_test.ts: out-of-range, unpadded, 13-digit, sign-prefixed and full-wi

  • Hyphenated names: a hyphen in a member chain on a known foreign root is read as part of the name, so ${{ matrix.node-version }} still passes through. CEL parses it as a subtraction.

A worker that reconnects before the orchestrator has seen its old socket close is unverified while dispatches sent on the old socket still hold its slots. The integration test "AccessDataPoller: a grant created by a real method run through A stays staged on A and reaches B" failed intermittently under full-suite load:

```

AssertionError: Values are not equal: A's own run stays staged

  • allow

+ deny

```

The test started poller A before the method run, on a 20 ms interval. A run writes grant-main, then publishes ModelUpdated several awaits later. A poll cycle on A that lands in that gap sees a version no own event has named yet and counts it as a peer change, which reloads the policy and applies the staged grant.

That is the documented fail-safe of FilesystemAccessDataChangeSource, and its unit tests pin it ("an own version seen before its event is a change"). It is not what this test is about, so the fix is in the test: poller A now starts once the run has finished. The change source is primed and listening before the run, so A's first cycle attributes the new version to the run's event.

The test still checks that the real event payload and the report written after it do not read as a peer change on A, and that B applies the grant. No product code changes.

Fixes swamp-club#3393.

Fixes swamp-club#3373: on S3 and GCS v2 datastores, a run whose model lock was force-released (swamp datastore lock release --force) pushed anyway. Its write overwrote the version the next lock holder had written, both runs exited 0, and one acknowledged write was lost.

Mechanism

  • Each clone allocates the next data version from its own cache (atomicAllocateVersionDir). After a breakglass, the old holder and the new holder both write version N+1 under the same key.
  • The overwrite itself is a plain put inside the extensions' sync, so the last writer wins.
  • Core never re-checked the lock before pushing.
  • The publish check (unpublishedTargets) only asks whether the version exists remotely, so it passed on the other run's object.

What changes

  • The check before each push.
  • acquireModelLocks reads each per-model lock with inspect() just after taking it. Inside each push attempt, before any upload, it reads the lock again.
  • If the lock is gone, being written, or names a different holder, hostname, pid or nonce than the first reading, the push is refused with ModelLockLostError (code model_lock_lost).
  • The second reading is compared with the backend's own first reading, not with this process's identity. Third-party registry locks write their own formats: GitLab

Summary

A model method declaring rollbackOnFailure: true failed whenever it ran as a workflow step, with rollbackVersions is not supported in composite repository. Workflow steps write through CompositeUnifiedDataRepository, whose four deferred-write methods threw unconditionally. This has been the case since rollbackOnFailure was added, so it is not a regression.

  • CompositeUnifiedDataRepository routes saveDeferred and finalizeVersionDeferred by data lifetime, as save does. A DeferredWriteReceipt carries no lifetime, so the composite remembers which store issued each unsettled deferred version and settles each receipt there.
  • Promotion runs persistent first, then ephemeral. It is ordered, not atomic across the two stores. Rollback attempts both stores even when one fails. A failed promotion keeps the issuing records so the rollback that follows still reaches the right store.
  • InMemoryUnifiedDataRepository catalogs a deferred version when it is promoted, so a promoted ephemeral write is visible to data queries. It releases a never-finalized allocation on rollback, and promotion gives such a version no latest marker.
  • InProcessExecutor is unchanged. With the composite no longer throwing, a failing method reports its own error.
  • design/primitives/data.md and models.md describe the routing and settle order.

Fixes swamp-club#3255.

What's Changed

  • feat(datastore): a fenced writer lease replaces the v3 writer lock, so a writer that lost it lands nothing (swamp-club#3359) (#3066)

Summary

Datastore rework Phase 4 C (swamp-club#3359, on #2865's plan). A v3 datastore's single writer now holds a fenced writer lease instead of Phase 3's FileLock, and every commit names its fence, so a writer that lost the lease (a zombie) can land nothing.

  • The lease (src/domain/datastore_v3/writer_lease.ts) is built on create-only control-plane records under _control/writer/: fence-<n> taken with putIfAbsent, a heartbeat, and a released marker. Taking over creates the next fence and never rewrites the current one, so no compare-and-swap is needed. A fence is never reused.
  • The store-wide writer fence. commits.db (schema 4) keeps the highest fence taken. Taking the lease raises it, and every append checks it inside its own transaction after the partition's rules, so a zombie's commit is refused on every partition with datastore_v3_writer_fenced.
  • Clocks never decide safety. Expiry (TTL plus a 10 s skew allowance) only decides when another writer may take over.
  • Unchanged behaviour:
  • The busy refusal keeps its message and code.
  • swamp datastore lock status|release act on the lease.
  • A dead holder on the same host is still taken over at once.
  • A live Phase 3 writer.lock refuses the lease during an upgrade.
  • **Serve takes the lease back once another writer is done.

What's Changed

  • fix(repo): the claude tool no longer hides a repo's own AGENTS.md behind a new CLAUDE.md (swamp-club#3346) (#3057)

Summary

Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md. swamp init --tool claude (also the default tool) always created a CLAUDE.md. So in a repo that keeps its rules in AGENTS.md, Claude read swamp's instructions and ignored the repo's own. If you deleted CLAUDE.md, swamp repo upgrade recreated it. Fixes swamp-club#3346.

The claude tool now looks at the repo before writing and picks a target. The first rule that matches wins:

1. .claude/rules/swamp.md exists, or CLAUDE.md is a symlink: write the rules file. Symlinking CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md is a setup Claude Code's docs recommend. Swamp no longer writes through that link.

2. CLAUDE.md already holds swamp's managed section: keep writing there. If the file holds nothing else and AGENTS.md has the repo's own content, add an @AGENTS.md import inside the managed section. This repairs repos this bug already hit.

3. AGENTS.md has the repo's own content and there is no CLAUDE.md: write .claude/rules/swamp.md. Claude Code loads rules files alongside AGENTS.md, and has done since 2.0.64.

4. Otherwise: write CLAUDE.md, byte-for-byte as before.

Swamp's Claude rules never go into AGENTS.md itself. Claude Code before 2.1.277, and some sessions before 2.1.281, read only CLAUDE.md files and rules, so they would lose swamp's rules

Docs changed: design/surfaces/agent-interface.md

What's Changed

  • fix(workflows): a forEach's iterations run in list order (swamp-club#3318) (#3043)

Problem

A forEach step's iterations ran in the order of their expanded names, not their place in the in list. Within one level, TopologicalSortService.sort broke weight ties by name with localeCompare, and every iteration carries its template step's weight. So operate-10 ran before operate-2, and a step named deploy-${{ self.env }} over prod, dev, staging ran dev, prod, staging. With concurrency: 1, a workflow whose items each depend on the one before skipped every item from the tenth on.

Fix

  • GraphNode takes an optional group: { key, index }. Within a level the sort orders by weight, then the group key in place of the name, then the index, then the name. This is a single total order, so it stays deterministic and invariant under input order.
  • The execution walk groups each real forEach iteration under its template step at its list position. Iterations stay together and run in list order. Plain steps, jobs and the other sort callers set no group and sort exactly as before.
  • design/primitives/workflows.md states the within-level order.

Testing

  • Sort unit tests: 12 index-named iterations, named iterations in non-alphabetical order, iterations among plain steps, weight still ordering grouped nodes.
  • Property test: the generator now produces groups, and the ordering invariant checks the four-part order across random graphs.
  • Execut

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3317.

A local swamp model method run --timeout (and swamp behavior run --timeout) whose timeout fired exited 0 and printed nothing: no output at all under --json, and nothing after the "Executing" line in log mode. The run record was correct (cancelled, timed out), but a script bounding a run with --timeout saw a success.

The dispatcher reserved a slot when the scheduler placed a step and kept that reservation until the dispatch finished, while the gateway listed the same dispatch in the worker's activeDispatchIds for its whole run. A --concurrency 2 worker with one dispatch running therefore looked full: a step that arrived mid-dispatch was queued despite a free slot, and failed with a queue timeout if the running dispatch outlasted --queue-timeout.

  • DispatchService releases the reservation in that callback. The release is idempotent and built per attempt inside the retry loop, so a retried step releases each attempt's reservation, and the finally still releases for an attempt that fails before reaching the gateway.
  • A dispatch that bypasses the scheduler (skipScheduler, used by the fleet probe) no longer releases a reservation it never took.
  • design/enablers/remote-execution.md describes the reservation: a slot is counted once.

Not a regression: multi-slot workers and the counted reservation arrived together in #1769.

Fixes swamp-club#3276 (moved from #3006). Before this change, if a remote-run WebSocket connect failed and the error contained no HTTP status or TLS problem, the CLI checked /health. If the server answered, it replaced the real error with Authentication failed — run: swamp auth server-login. Dropped connections, early closes and serve's own 429s were all reported as auth failures, and the real cause was lost.

Most likely cause of the reporter's loopback failures (reproduced live): all loopback calls come from 127.0.0.1, so they hit serve's per-IP burst limit of 50 per minute. Over wss://, Deno's WebSocket client negotiates HTTP/2, which hides serve's 429. The /health guess then turned it into "Authentication failed", and serve's log showed zero token rejections, matching the report.

Change (src/cli/remote_run.ts): when a handshake fails without a status, the CLI repeats the handshake once as an HTTP/1.1 request without the token and classifies the error from the status serve returns:

| Probe result | Message |

|---|---|

| no answer | original error |

| 429 / 5xx | rate-limited / server error |

| 401/403, no token sent | Authentication failed — run: swamp auth server-login … (unchanged) |

| 401/403, token sent over wss:// | same auth message plus the original error (a token rejection can hide behind HTTP/2) |

| 401/40

  • Compaction point (store-wide). compactHistory(through) folds every commit at or below the point into a compacted base in commits.db, then deletes those commits. The base holds present records, live versions, catalog rows and forwards, file ownership and compacted seqs. It runs in batches of 250, one transaction each. A crash leaves each batch either whole or absent.
  • Retries. A compacted commit's txnId moves to compacted_txns, so a retry still returns duplicate. Each compacted partition gets a snapshot at its compacted seq.
  • Catch-up. A checkout behind the point gets CommitsCompactedError. It then loads the base, reconciling its files, _catalog_v3.db and state, and replays only the commits after the point. A load that fails part-way converges, even against a newer base.
  • GC reference rule. chunk_refs becomes a count of the surviving commits and base records that name each chunk. A chunk whose last reference is compacted away counts as released and stays referenced for the sweep's grace period.

  • saved nothing;
  • ran none of its always/completed cleanup steps;

swamp now sends a stop request on Windows, the equivalent of SIGTERM from one swamp process to another:

  • Listener (src/infrastructure/process/windows_stop_request.ts): a named auto-reset kernel32 event, Local\swamp-stop-<pid>, polled every 100ms on an unref'd timer.
  • Each subscription has its own idempotent end.
  • A failed create leaves no state behind.
  • The event is drained once at creation, so a stale request aimed at a reused pid is ignored.
  • A handler that throws doesn't keep the request from the other subscribers.
  • registerShutdownHandler: on Windows, it listens for stop requests where it would register SIGTERM on POSIX. No call sites change.
  • killProcessTree: sends the stop

Adata and output repositories stage typed changes on v3 (swamp-club#3250) (#2994)

`feat` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-11T17:57:24Zdatastorefeat

What's Changed

  • feat(datastore): data and output repositories stage typed changes on v3 (swamp-club#3250) (#2994)

Summary

Datastore rework Phase 3 (swamp-club#3250, tracking swamp-club#2865), dormant until the v3 opt-in. This is the first of three repository staging groups. It adds the shared typed staging route, and makes the data and output repositories stage typed changes on v3 for every write they make. v2 behaviour does not change.

1. The shared route, and why it costs v2 nothing

A repository makes two calls (src/infrastructure/persistence/unit_of_work_scope.ts):

  • Before the write: signalChange(markDirty, pathChange, { typed: true }), the same call as today.
  • On v2 the option changes nothing.
  • In a bound unit that takes typed changes, the path change is checked but not staged. A write outside a bound unit is still refused before anything is written.
  • After the write: stageTyped(markDirty, build), once per batch.
  • On v2 it returns after one requiresUnit lookup, and build never runs. The test stageTyped: a builder never runs on v2: no hook, route 2, or a legacy unit covers this.
  • On a v3 hook with no bound unit it throws UnscopedWriteRefusedError before building.

The issue sketched a single pre-write call with a lazy builder. That can't work: the version, the content and whether the latest marker moved are all only known after the write, and moving the call after the write would change v2's pre-write signal timing.

What's Changed

Summary

Dormant chunk garbage collection for the v3 datastore: it reclaims chunks no commit names (left by abandoned units, refused or failed commits, and crashes between storing chunks and committing), finds damaged chunks, and removes the filesystem storage's orphaned temp files. Nothing in production calls it; a v3 datastore gc wires it in at the opt-in.

The reference set is the commit log, not chunksInUse

A fresh checkout catching up from cursor 0 replays every commit and reads every chunk each put names, including content later overwritten, deleted or garbage-collected. Deleting any of those would stop the catch-up permanently with ChunkMissingError. chunksInUse describes one checkout's present records at its own cursor, so it cannot be the reference set. A chunk is kept for as long as any stored commit names it.

The chunk index and its migration

  • commits.db schema 2 adds chunk_refs(namespace, sha256), written in each append's own transaction, so a refused, repeated or rolled-back append writes none.
  • Commit.chunkRefs() / BlobRef.chunkHashes() define what a commit names: the whole-content hash for one chunk, every part's hash otherwise.
  • The migration from version 1 backfills the table in SQL from the stored bodies. Malformed bodies are skipped instead of failing the open, and are still reported as corruption on rebuild. Indexing too muc

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3241. On Windows, Deno turns every signal into TerminateProcess, which ends one process and leaves its children running. So when swamp workflow cancel or swamp model cancel stopped a run's owner, or a supervisor stopped swamp serve, the step's powershell (running Start-Sleep) survived. The survivors held files open (os error 32 on cleanup) and serve's inherited stdout/stderr, so anything waiting on serve's output hung until the step finished.

Each shell step on Windows now runs in a kill-on-close Job Object (src/infrastructure/process/windows_job.ts, kernel32 via FFI):

  • When the swamp process dies: for any reason, its job handles close and Windows ends every step process tree. This covers cancel and serve stop with one mechanism.
  • On abort or timeout: the job is terminated after the existing taskkill /T, so the walk still starts from the live child. The job then sweeps descendants the walk can't reach.
  • When a step exits on its own: kill-on-close is cleared before the job closes, so what the step deliberately backgrounded keeps running, as on POSIX. Breakaway is allowed for programs that ask for it.
  • When a job can't be made: the step runs without one, as today.

process_kill.ts and the cancel commands are unchanged.

This follows the same pattern as the handlers' pullBeforeTokenWrite. If the pull fails, it throws before anything is deleted.
  • Design doc. design/primitives/serve.md is updated: the gap description is removed, and it now describes the lock and pull the GC takes, their cost, and what MAX_TOKENS_PER_SWEEP does and does not bound.

The same redactor backs issue bug/feature/security/edit/ripple, so all of them get the fix.

Inside markdown code (fenced blocks and inline code spans), an FQDN match is now kept as written when:

  • its last label is one of name, info, run, page, site, jobs (TLDs that are also everyday property names), and
  • it lies wholly inside a closed code range, and

Everything else is redacted as before: hosts on ordinary or country TLDs (com, net, io, it, in, id, …) including inside code, hosts in URL/userinfo/port context, secrets, IPs, emails and internal hosts, and all prose.

The code-range scanner fails toward redacting: unclosed fences and spans, escaped backticks, invalid fence openers, indented code blocks and multi-line spans are all treated as prose. Fence scanning stops at the first unclosed fence, which keeps it linear.

Accepted trade-off

Summary

Closes swamp-club#2867, the follow-up to swamp-club#2736. Ending a parent run used to leave its suspended nested runs as they were: still listed for approval, still resumable, with nothing left to read their outcome.

Cascade. Cancelling, rejecting or superseding a suspended parent now cancels the suspended child runs it waited on, and theirs, to the nesting limit.

  • Only a child linked both ways is followed, and each is cancelled under its own claim after being read again.
  • A child with a live owner, one that does not link back, or one whose record is not the datastore's copy is left and reported with its cancel command.
  • Through serve the children are cancelled in the parent's gated unit of work, so one push carries them. A child the instance is running is asked to stop and is not waited for.
  • The cascade never writes the parent, and one child's failure does not stop the rest.

Backstop on the child. A suspended nested run whose parent ended, or whose parent step moved on to another child, refuses approve, reject and resume and cancels itself. Recover and signal delivery reach it through resume.

  • A parent that cannot be read, has no record, holds a malformed link, or differs from the datastore's copy refuses and writes nothing.
  • The run's own record is confirmed against the datastore before the cancel is wr

  • Validation: workflow validate refuses the same key on two steps of a workflow and a key on a step under forEach, naming the steps.

  • Claims: numbered write-once records in the control-plane store, wait-keys/<workflowId>/<key>/<generation>, created with putIfAbsent as continuation claims are. The holder is the wait of the highest claim for as long as that wait has no outcome. The S3 and GCS datastore extensions need no change.

What's Changed

  • feat(serve): run scheduled workflows concurrently and report queue delay (swamp-club#3046) (#2955)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3046.

swamp serve runs every scheduled workflow through one global queue, one run at a time, and no setting changes that. On the reporter's serve, each run spends about 37 s in datastore sync. Once a per-minute schedule was added, the queue saturated: a 40 */6 * * * fire started 2 h 49 min late, and a 2-59/5 schedule ran half its fires. Health only shows running, so none of this waiting was visible.

New setting: max-concurrent-scheduled-runs. Available as a config key, the SWAMP_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCHEDULED_RUNS env var and the --max-concurrent-scheduled-runs flag on serve and serve daemon enable. It is separate from --max-concurrent-runs, which limits API runs.

  • Default is 1, which keeps today's behaviour: one scheduled run at a time, in fire order.
  • Above 1, the scheduler starts the first queued run whose workflow isn't already running. Different workflows run together; a workflow never overlaps itself. A cron fire (keyed by workflow id) and a replayed run (keyed by name) count as the same workflow.

Queue delay in health.

  • Each schedule in the health snapshot, /health and the dashboard now reports queued, oldestQueuedAt and lastQueueDelayMs.
  • schedule_started carries queueDelayMs.
  • All queue data is per schedule, so the per-token health view filters it along with its schedule

What's Changed

  • feat(serve): settle expired signal waits from the continuation sweep (swamp-club#3109) (#2943)

Summary

Under swamp serve nothing looked at a wait_for_signal deadline, so an expired wait stayed suspended and its failed handlers did not run until someone resumed the run (swamp-club#3109, split out of swamp-club#3094).

  • The continuation sweep settles expired waits. When continueSettledRun finds a run held back only by its waits, settleExpiredWaits settles each wait that is past its deadline, has no outcome and is still registered, through the write-once create. The run then continues on the path a signalled run takes, so the resume fails the step with wait_timeout and failed handlers run with no client action.
  • --max-signal-wait-timeout on serve (env SWAMP_MAX_SIGNAL_WAIT_TIMEOUT, config key max-signal-wait-timeout, at most one year). A step that asks for a longer wait fails when it would open the wait. A wait already open keeps its deadline.

Behaviour to know

  • Timeouts follow the workflow's auto-resume policy, as signals do. A workflow serve may not resume keeps its expired wait unsettled and its run suspended.
  • The sweep settles only a wait whose registration can still be read, so a suspended copy of a run that ended or was deleted elsewhere never gets an outcome.
  • Each instance reads the deadline against its own clock and the first create wins, so serve hosts need synchronised clocks. There is no skew allowance.

  • A resume that starts and fails is retried with a backoff from 30s to 15m, per suspension.

Summary

When several swamp processes started at once in a fresh repo, one could log:

```

[WRN] Catalog migration to per-extension-aggregate-v3 failed (Error: database is locked …); falling back to cold-start rebuild

[WRN] Catalog cold-start rebuild complete; loaders will repopulate from disk on next access

```

runDataMigrationTransaction opened a deferred BEGIN, read the catalog, then blocked on its first write. When another process committed meanwhile, the stale WAL snapshot failed with database is locked, and busy_timeout does not retry that. The catch treated the error as a data failure: it warned and ran the cold-start rebuild, which empties the catalog. On a fresh catalog that is only noise. On a populated pre-v3 catalog being upgraded, it would wipe every row and force a full re-import.

The migration now:

  • takes the write lock up front with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, as CatalogStore already does;
  • re-checks its marker under the lock, and skips work another process committed while it waited;
  • rolls back and rethrows lock errors, so initializeWithRetry retries them with backoff, as its docs already said it did.

Only real migration failures still fall back to the cold-start rebuild.

Without managedConfig the behaviour is unchanged: one attempt, a WARN, and serve starts.

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#2844 and swamp-club#3162. Both bugs are in swamp datastore setup (src/libswamp/datastores/setup.ts).

swamp-club#2844: setup overwrote a remote config tier

On a managedConfig repo whose .swamp/config is the config tier, datastore setup extension copied that tier into the cache and pushed it before pulling anything. If the remote already held a config tier, for example when a second repo joins a shared datastore that was already migrated, the push overwrote the team's definitions, upstream_extensions.json and the managed-config-migrated.json sentinel. Each file went to whichever repo wrote it last.

What setup does now:

  • Pulls the remote config first. It pulls only config/ (subdirs: ["config"], with the namespace, and metadataOnly under lazy hydration) before any copy, within the setup sync timeout.
  • Stops on a failed pull, including a timeout. Nothing moves and .swamp.yaml is not rewritten. A timeout has to stop setup too: committing the new datastore without migrating would make a retry classify the tier as instance-local.
  • The remote copy wins. planConfigTierMerge, a pure function in datastore_config.ts, decides what happens to each file the local tier and the cache both hold:
  • Shared files are not copied, so they are never pushed.

Summary

A nested structural swamp (for example swamp data gc) skips the per-model locks named in its inherited lock list, on the assumption that the holder waits on it and writes nothing until it exits. That stopped being true when the hop the lock was lent to ended with something still running under it:

  • a dispatch that is cancelled before the worker has killed its runner;
  • a worker that is lost, whose step is dispatched again under the same lock;
  • a shell command that killed the --server client it started, or left a swamp in the background.

The leftover swamp kept skipping the lock while the holder wrote (swamp-club#3111). The --server path was reproduced against a loopback swamp serve; the two dispatch paths were traced in the code.

The holder cannot confirm that what it started is dead: a worker kills only the runner process, a partitioned worker confirms nothing, and a run requested over --server is meant to outlive a dropped socket. So the holder acts on its own lock instead.

Changes

  • Hand-offs. A run lends its locks to a hop through a hand-off: LockHolderMarker.beginChildHandOff for a shell command, and beginLockHandOff on RemoteStepRequest, one per dispatch attempt. Whoever begins one awaits its end when the hop returns and before the run writes.

  • The drain counts a fresh unreadable per-model lock as held. It cannot tell whose lock it is, so it is never skipped as an ancestor's; a nested command waits one poll and then reads it normally.

The orchestrator holds a step's per-model lock while a remote worker runs the step.   • Worker: when the hostname is its own, it puts the pid at the front of the dispatch runner's SWAMP_LOCK_ANCESTOR_PIDS and the nonces into SWAMP_LOCK_HOLDER_TOKENS. The nested swamp then skips exactly the dispatched step's locks and still waits on every other lock the orchestrator holds.
  • Validation: the field is bounded by the dispatch schema and checked again by withRemoteLockHolder, which never adds the pid without its tokens entry.
  • Compatibility: the field is optional, so REMOTE_PROTOCOL_VERSION is unchanged. An older worker ignores it and an older orchestrator never sends it.

Two parallel workflow steps, or two concurrent runs, that each start a nested structural command (swamp data gc, datastore sync, and so on) wait on each other. Each nested drain skips its own run's per-model lock and waits on the other run's, and each run keeps its lock until its nested command exits. Both used to fail at SWAMP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS.

Now one of them fails within seconds and the other proceeds.

  • Drain-wait markers. A drain that has to wait publishes a short-lived marker under drain-waits/ in the datastore. It names the locks the drain skips (held for it until it exits) and the locks it waits on, by lock-file nonce.
  • Mutual wait. Two drains wait on each other when each waits on a lock the other skips. A drain nested deeper in the same run skips those locks too, so it is waited for, not failed.
  • Who yields. Drains are ordered by start time, then id. A drain yields when it mutually waits with an earlier drain that is not itself yielding, so of a group that all wait on each other exactly one keeps waiting.

Deno refuses every /proc path unless the process has --allow-all, which neither the compiled binary nor the test and dev tasks have. Both Linux probes in src/infrastructure/runtime/process.ts went through Deno and so never worked there:

Both now read /proc through libc over FFI (--allow-ffi is already granted), the route process_ancestry.ts takes for the same restriction. isProcessGone falls through to the SIGURG probe when the entry is absent or libc cannot be loaded.

The two fixes ship together on purpose: turning liveness on while the identity still lacked the namespace would let one container roll back another's in-flight write.

Acquisition is now all-or-nothing: any throw in the per-model loop releases the locks this call registered and rethrows the original error. That covers three paths:

  • the step-start pull failing (the reported case)
  • the global lock re-check after an acquire throwing
  • a later model's lock acquire failing after earlier locks were taken

The error text and the returned lock result are unchanged, and no caller changes. Most of the diff in src/cli/repo_context.ts is the loop body being reindented inside the try; git diff -w shows the roughly 20 lines that matter.

Summary

At serve startup, WalSink.replay wrote each WAL segment left from the previous session to StoreSink and deleted it straight away. StoreSink.write only buffers below the batch size, so the segment was gone before any store put. A failed put or an exit before the next flush lost those events from both the WAL and the store.

A run whose abort lands before a lone job's level no longer reaches an approval gate and suspends. It ends cancelled

What doesn't change. Stdout, exit codes and log mode are unchanged. An error with no held warning is byte-identical to before. design/surfaces/auth-gate.md is updated to match.

Trade-off. In --json mode, long-running serve and worker connect now write the warning at shutdown rather than at startup. The previous release wrote no JSON-mode warning at all.

#2781 handed down whichever proof the parent's pass rested on. In CI that was usually the SWAMP_SIGNIN_TOKEN proof, so SWAMP_NESTED_GATE_PASS was <pid>. followed by the token itself, visible to every shell-step child.

Now the handoff is a fresh whoami proof, else the valid auth_verified.json proof, and never the signin-token proof (validFileProof in src/cli/auth_gate.ts).

  • In CI, the first gated run of a job checks the token live and caches a fresh proof, so later runs have a file proof to hand down.
  • A run that passed offline on its token alone hands down nothing.

2. Nested proofs had no expiry bound

#2781 skipped exp in nested mode, so a leaked proof worked indefinitely under any live swamp ancestor.

Now a nested proof must carry an exp later than the issuing ancestor's start time (admitsNestedRun in src/domain/auth/nested_gate_pass.ts).

  • The start time is read from the OS: /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 plus btime on Linux, proc_bsdinfo.pbi_start_tvsec on macOS. It matches ps to th

This applies to managedConfig repos on an S3 or GCS datastore. Extension writes changed the cached copy of config/upstream_extensions.json without fetching it first, then pushed it. The datastore stores each file last-writer-wins, so a write from a stale cache erased entries that other checkouts had added:

  • a stale extension rm reverted a peer's addition;
  • concurrent pulls kept only one of the two entries.

Extension writes now run in a managed lockfile transaction (src/libswamp/extensions/managed_lockfile_transaction.ts). Downloads still happen outside any lock. Then, under the datastore global lock, the transaction:

1. fetches the lockfile with a config-scoped pull;

2. replays any change an earlier transaction failed to publish;

3. applies the change;

4. records the outstanding change as a pending delta, publishes exactly the lockfile, and clears the record.

What goes through it, and what changed alongside:

  • Callers: the CLI's extension pull, update, rm, search-install, install, repo upgrade and doctor extensions --repair, plus serve's extension handlers. The old unlocked post-command publish is gone.

Agive serve and worker background work their own traces (swamp-club#2467) (#2763)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-01T09:59:07Ztracingfix

What's Changed

  • fix(tracing): give serve and worker background work their own traces (swamp-club#2467) (#2763)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#2467. swamp serve runs inside a swamp.cli span that ends only when serve exits, and the AsyncLocalStorage context manager carried it into every timer serve started. So every poll cycle, scheduled fire and background loop joined one trace per process, which grew to millions of spans under a root that was never exported. This PR gives each unit of background work its own trace, applies the same fix to workers, and fixes span export at process exit.

Serve

  • Poll cycles: each cycle (config, access_data, runtime_data, grants_directory) is the root of its own swamp.serve.poll trace, tagged with swamp.serve.poller. Its sync-gate wait, datastore sync and extension spans (for example S3 getObject) nest under the cycle.

3. Unset HOME (1 test, fails every run). The mixed runtime expressions test read env["HOME"], which Windows runners don't set. It now reads a variable supplied through withMockedEnv.

What's Changed

  • perf(datastore): a fresh v3 checkout catches up without an fsync per file (swamp-club#3337) (#3048)

Summary

A fresh filesystem-v3 checkout of 1,000 items took 26 s on macOS against v2's 1.1 s. The read model fsynced every file and directory it wrote, one at a time, and on macOS each fsync is a full drive-cache flush (F_FULLFSYNC).

  • Pages, not commits. Commits apply a page at a time. Each commit's state transaction is a savepoint in one transaction for the page, which commits after the page's barrier. An apply error keeps the commits before it, as before.
  • No fsync during a catch-up where the kernel names the boot. A written file can only be lost to an OS crash or power loss, and either ends the boot. The state records the keys each commit wrote or removed, in that commit's own transaction, together with the boot: boot_id on Linux, kern.bootsessionuuid on macOS (never the clock). The first open in a later boot checks each listed file against the state (SHA-256, or absence). A mismatch, or a file it cannot read, resets the state and replays every commit; otherwise the list is cleared. Where the boot cannot be named (Windows, or the read fails), each page is synced at its barrier instead.
  • DurableWriteBatch writes through temp file and rename. When it syncs (the compacted-base load, recovery's sweep, no boot id), it fsyncs the files and then each touched directory once, deepest first, with bounded parallelism. A removal syncs t

Summary

The Adversarial Review, CI Security Review and Review Integrity gates read the last github-actions review whose body started with ## <Heading>, on any commit. Claude Code refuses a quoted Bash argument containing a line that starts with #, so reviewers retried until a bold-heading variant got through. The gates skipped the bold review and read an older one. On #3091 a passing review was blocked by a stale CHANGES_REQUESTED on an older commit. The same flaw could also let an older pass stand in for a newer bold failure.

Fixes swamp-club#3425 (cause) and swamp-club#3422 (symptom).

  • Fail steps keep only the review whose .commit.oid is the PR head commit (HEAD_SHA set through env). They pass on APPROVED or COMMENTED, fail on CHANGES_REQUESTED, and fail when no review was posted for the head commit.
  • Heading match is ^(#+ |\*\*)?<Heading>, so #, ##, bold and plain headings are all recognised.
  • Skip checks read state and commit from one selection instead of two calls.
  • Prompts post the body with gh pr review N … --body-file - <<'EOF', which the permission check allows.

What's Changed

  • fix(ci): fail closed when auto-merge prerequisites were cancelled or skipped (swamp-club#3048) (#3019)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3048. The Auto-merge PR job could merge a core-source PR whose adversarial review never ran.

The gate was !failure() && !cancelled(), which only asks whether anything failed:

  • When a runner outage cancelled Detect Changes, every review was skipped. A skipped job doesn't count as a failure.
  • A review cancelled on its own, whether by an outage or by the next push's concurrency group, is cancelled without cancelling the run, so cancelled() stayed false.

In both cases the merge job still qualified.

This change makes the gate fail closed:

  • auto-merge now needs changes. It requires success from changes, validate-attestation and every review, and accepts a skipped review only when the matching changes output (core, ci, trust_root) says that review wasn't required.
  • !cancelled() stays as the status function, so GitHub doesn't add its implicit success() and a cancelled run never merges.
  • gh pr merge passes --match-head-commit, so a run only merges the commit it checked. An older run can no longer merge a newer push whose review hasn't finished.
  • integration/ci_merge_gate_rules_test.ts pins the gate so it can't be quietly reverted.

Datastore rework Phase 4A (swamp-club#3357, on #2865's plan). This adds the "Phase 4A: replication cost on a bucket model" section to design/enablers/datastore-litestream.md and makes datastores.md agree with it. The PR changes docs only.

On the bucket model. The issue asked for real S3 and GCS buckets. The issue's author (stack72, the maintainer) decided this spike would use emulators instead: ministack and fake-gcs-server behind a proxy that models latency, TLS handshakes, bandwidth and credential delays. The record says this up front. The choice rests on request, byte and connection counts, which don't depend on the emulator. A real-bucket check is listed as a gate before Phase 4E.

  • Choice for 4D: an idle sidecar, not one per command.
  • A per-command sidecar never runs Litestream's compaction or retention. A day's replica of 252 objects took 18 s to restore at 20 ms round trip and 121 s at 150 ms, against 1.1 s and 5.7 s once compacted.
  • It also pays new connections and credentials on every command.
  • An idle sidecar adds 24–283 ms to a write command.
  • Waiting for replication is acceptable. With an idle sidecar, a small v3 write that waits is 2–11 times faster than the v2 push it replaces. Every write measured is faster: 1.9–14 times.
  • Teardown order, traced and fixed. Th

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3348: startStartServer: two agent opens at once open only one window occasionally opened 3 windows under parallel load.

The server dedupes correctly: a second launch, resume or agent open joins the in-flight one as soon as the server reads its message. The test released the held launcher right after *sending* the second tab's request, without waiting for the server to *read* it. Under load the first open could finish and clear its in-flight entry first, so the second request opened a new window.

  • Adds a Client.dispatched() barrier. It sends an unrecognised request and awaits its invalid_request reply, which the server sends as soon as it reads the message. A socket's messages are read in order, so the reply proves every earlier request on that socket was dispatched. (start.status can't be used here because it queues behind the held launch.)
  • Uses it in the reported test and in two sibling tests with the same race: two launches at once open only one window, and a launch or resume refuses to run on a task another tab opened meanwhile. The latter now has the fixed queue order launch, task open, resume.

Test-only change; no src/ changes.

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3343. Two read-model tests added in #3048 (swamp-club#3337) failed on a Linux host with AssertionError: Expected function to reject:

  • read model: a commit whose unsynced keys cannot be recorded is not recorded as applied
  • read model: when SQLite rolls a page back itself, the error that caused it is the one reported

Both tests add a trigger that refuses inserts into unsynced_keys and expect catch-up to reject. They opened the read model without a boot identity, so they used the host's (/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on Linux). On a host where that can't be read, the read model syncs every file instead of recording unsynced keys, which is the designed behaviour. The trigger never fired, and catch-up succeeded.

Both tests now pass a fixed bootIdentity, the way the other swamp-club#3337 tests already do. No product code changes.

2026-10-11T00:30:42Zdesigndocs

What's Changed

  • docs(design): Litestream embedding decision record for the v3 datastore (swamp-club#3234) (#2976)

Summary

Decision record from the datastore rework Phase 3 Litestream spike (swamp-club#3234, tracking swamp-club#2865). Docs only: design/enablers/datastore-litestream.md, linked from design/enablers/datastores.md and the design/README.md enablers index.

  • Embedding: run the upstream litestream binary as a supervised sidecar, embedded with deno compile --include and SHA-256-verified on every start. Rejected: the Go c-shared library (it would put a second SQLite copy inside swamp's process), a TypeScript reimplementation, LiteFS, and the session extension.
  • Outbox rule: a commit is replicated once a control-socket /sync {"wait": true} call that started after it returns synced or no_change with replicated_txid >= txid.
  • commits.db checkpoints: keep SQLite's default checkpointing and never force one. A forced TRUNCATE made the replica 11× larger.
  • Shutdown and crash: the shutdown sync is unreliable, so writers always force a sync before stopping. Nothing confirmed was lost in any kill -9 run.
  • Failover: one replica path per writer fence. A shared path corrupted the replica in 4 of 4 runs.
  • Windows: needs Litestream 0.5.18, which is unreleased (litestream#1542 / #1548). Deno has no AF_UNIX client on Windows, so swamp uses litestream sync as the client there. If 0.5.18 isn't out, Windows solo stays on v2

Cpin that a resume refused on an open wait leaves no continuation claim (swamp-club#3183) (#2940)

`test` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-08T18:23:58Zworkflowstest

What's Changed

  • test(workflows): pin that a resume refused on an open wait leaves no continuation claim (swamp-club#3183) (#2940)

Summary

swamp-club#3183 reported that a manual swamp workflow resume on a run whose wait_for_signal is still open keeps the continuation claim on an unchanged suspension key, so serve never continues the run once it is signalled.

The report did not reproduce, and this PR changes no behaviour. takeOverRun refuses an open wait before it claims the suspension, so the refused resume leaves no claim behind. What was missing was a test for that ordering on signal waits (only approval gates had one) and an accurate statement of the invariant the suspension key relies on.

  • New test (execution_service_test.ts): a resume refused on an open wait leaves the run suspended on the same key with no claim; after the wait is settled, an automatic resume by a serve holder takes the claim and finishes the run.
  • Extra assertion (continuation_claim_test.ts): applying an accepted signal gives the run a new suspension key.
  • Comments and design doc: suspensionKeyOf, the claim site in takeOverRun, and design/primitives/workflows.md now say that a resume which *takes the claim* changes a step, because one that would not is refused first.

Neither fix proposed in the issue (releasing the claim on an unchanged key, or a per-resume counter in the key) is implemented, since nothing reaches that state today.

2026-10-06T21:45:09Zdesigndocs

What's Changed

  • docs(design): vault.get expressions are an author capability over serve (swamp-club#3086) (#2888)

Summary

Closes swamp-club#3086 as by design and records the rule in design/enablers/access-control.md (section "Expression references").

  • New "Vault secrets" rule. A vault.get(...) expression is an author's capability and is not checked against grants on any serve path. Writers (write on the model or workflow) may use any vault secret in what they author. Unlike env, model method run inputs may carry vault.get(...) from any caller (run-only CI tokens rely on this); the value reaches the method and is masked in output. So write on workflows or models, and run on a model whose method can surface its inputs, include access to the repo's vault secrets.
  • Distinguishes the expression from the vault.get serve request, which is authorized (read on data:vault).
  • Workflow run inputs are inert and never resolve the expression.
  • Replaces the old "vault authorization is swamp-club#2676" note; per-vault scoping stays with swamp-club#2676.

Data references in the same issue were already fixed by #2878 (write-time checks against the writer). No behaviour change in this PR: docs only. User manual follow-up is swamp-club#3115.

Test Plan

  • Docs only; no source, test, skill or UAT changes.
  • Claims checked against the code: src/domain/expressions/expression_references.ts records no vault reference, authorizeExpressionReferences only gat

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#2921. The swamp skill's execution-semantics reference said that cancelling a run cancels the child runs of its nested workflow steps. It also said a child run can't be cancelled by its own id over --server. Both statements are only true while the parent is still running.

This PR rewrites the paragraph in .claude/skills/swamp/references/workflow/references/execution-semantics.md to cover both cases:

  • Running parent (swamp-club#2470): the cancel reaches the nested children. Over --server, cancel the parent's run id, because serve does not register a running child under its own id.
  • Parent suspended on a nested run (swamp-club#2736), then cancelled or superseded:
  • The nested step fails with Detached: the run ended while this step waited on … and the child stays suspended.
  • The output warns that the child was left unfinished and prints the command that cancels it. In --json this is detachedNestedRuns[].cancelCommand.
  • You cancel the child under its own workflow name and run id, adding --server <url> when serve owns it. Serve does cancel a suspended child by its own id.
  • The text links to nested-workflows.md and notes that swamp-club#2867 tracks making the cancel cascade to the child.
